anti_overlap: Defers to fd-staged-dispatch-correctness on dispatch ordering; defers to fd-expansion-signal-quality on expansion scoring
decision_lens: Budget accounting must remain accurate after tier adjustments — no silent cost drift
focus: Validate that cross-model dispatch interacts correctly with existing budget enforcement and cost estimation
name: fd-budget-integration
persona: Cost optimization engineer who manages token budgets across multi-agent dispatch
review_areas: Cost estimate update — when a Stage 2 agent is downgraded from sonnet to haiku, does the budget tracker reflect the lower token estimate?
Budget pressure computation — is remaining_budget / sum(stage2_estimates) calculated before or after tier adjustment?
Circular dependency: budget pressure influences tier → tier influences cost estimate → cost estimate influences budget pressure
Interaction with AgentDropout — if dropout saves tokens, does that increase remaining budget for tier decisions?
estimate-costs.sh integration — does it have per-model cost data, or only per-agent averages?

severity_examples.condition: Budget not updated after tier adjustment
severity_examples.scenario: Budget tracker shows Stage 2 at sonnet cost but agents actually run at haiku

severity_examples.condition: No fixed-point iteration or one-pass guarantee
severity_examples.scenario: Circular dependency causes oscillation — agent downgraded, budget improves, agent upgraded, budget worsens

severity_examples.condition: Dropout and expansion scoring use independent budget snapshots
severity_examples.scenario: AgentDropout savings not reflected in budget pressure calculation

success_hints: Single-pass pipeline: dropout → budget snapshot → expansion scoring → tier adjustment → cost update. No feedback loops.
task_context: budget.yaml defines per-category token defaults. estimate-costs.sh queries interstat for historical per-agent costs. Budget enforcement is currently a binary gate (launch or defer).
